lines.title: For this chapter, please prepare:
2.5mm Allen key
T10 key / screwdriver
Flush cutters - an optional tool, recommended to use for cutting the zip ties. It can be purchased from our e-shop prusa3d.com.
For this chapter, we also recommend printing out the community-made Snap-rivet-remover
We recommend removing the Bowden-guide to make the zip tie insertion easier in the next step.
Remove the M3x10 screw that secures the Bowden-guide part in the right rear corner of the printer.
Remove the Bowden-guide. We will not need it anymore.
Remove the eleven nylon rivets that keep the right side cover attached to the printer.
You can use the core-one-snap-rivet-remover mentioned in the previous step.
Carefully remove the side cover and set it aside for now.
Set the side cover aside for now.
For the following steps, prepare:
Side-handle-right (1x) found in the Wiper bag
M3nN nut (2x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
M3x8rT screw (2x) you removed earlier
Right side cover (1x) you removed earlier
Insert two M3x8rT screw into the Side-handle-right.
Align the Side-handle-right with the holes in the right side panel and place it in position.
Place M3nN nuts onto the screws and hold them with the universal tool.
Firmly tighten the screws from the other side.
For the following steps, prepare:
Wiper-base (1x) found in the Wiper bag
Note that the Wiper-base in the photos may differ slightly from the delivered part. This does not affect the assembly or functionality.
Wiper-lock (1x) found in the Wiper bag
Wiper-adjuster (1x) found in the Wiper bag
Silicone wiper (1x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag

Nozzle cleaner is the name for the whole assembly.
M3nN nut (1x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
M3x8rT screw (1x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
M3x20rT screw (1x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
M3x12rT screw (2x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
Push the M3x20rT screw through the Wiper-lock.
Insert the Wiper-lock with the screw into the Wiper-base.
From the opposite side, place the M3nN nut onto the screw and tighten it using the universal wrench.
Loosen it by a quarter to half a turn so the Wiper-lock can move.
Set the Wiper-lock according to the markings on the Wiper-base.
If the Wiper-lock moves on its own, slightly tighten the screw.
Insert the M3x8rT screw through the channel in the Wiper-base.
Align the hole in the Wiper-adjuster with the screw.
Secure the Wiper-adjuster in the slots using the universal wrench and tighten the M3x8rT screw with a T10 screwdriver.
Do not fully tighten so the Wiper-adjuster can be turned.
Note the irregular shape of the Wiper-adjuster. Use the universal wrench to position it so that its flattened side faces downward.
Insert the silicone priming block into the front slot (left in the photo). Ensure the part is oriented correctly.
Insert the silicone wiper into the rear slot (right in the photo).
Check the correct position of the silicone wiper. The wiper is sloped; make sure that the sloped side points inside the Wiper-base.
Pro tip: Lightly wipe the wiper blocks with IPA (Isopropyl alcohol) before inserting and securing them in the wiper base. This will make the insertion a lot easier.
Secure the silicone wiper and priming block with two M3x12rT screws.
Guide the T10 key or screwdriver through the dedicated openings in the Wiper-base for better access.
Double-check that the wiper is inserted correctly, with the sloped side pointing inside the Wiper-base.
Insert the wiper assembly into the hole in the side cover-right.
Turn the lock to keep the wiper assembly attached to the cover.
Set the side cover with the attached wiper assembly aside for now; we will mount it onto the printer soon.
For the following steps, prepare:
Zip tie (3x)
The dock fan cable connector is the remaining part of the head cable.
Insert the Dock fan cable connector through the lower oval opening on the left side of the rear panel.
Push the cable inside.
Inside the printer, gently pull the dock fan cable as shown in the photo.
Some of our printers do not have the grommet on the lower opening. This does not affect the process.

steps.title: Leading the dock fan cable I.

lines.title: Note the three pairs of holes on the right side of the printer.
Move the INDX Toolhead to the front, between the front and the middle holes on the right side.
Insert one zip tie into the rear hole as shown in the photo.
Make sure that the zip tie is NOT looped around the belts!
Ensure that the zip tie is led as shown in the photo and that it is not looped around the smooth rod.
Attach the other two zip ties in the same way.
Check again that the cable is led correctly behind the rod holder and above the smooth rod.
Connect all three zip ties as shown in the photo. Do not tighten them yet.
Lead the dock fan cable through all three connected zip ties.
Move the end of the Dock fan cable inside the printer. Do not loop it around the front right profile.
Lead the dock fan cable through the opening between the core XY and the printer's frame.
Before tightening the zipties, ensure that the dock fan cable is in position and protruding 8 cm/3.14 inches.
Ensure that the cable is not slack between the zip ties.
Tighten the zip ties.
Move the INDX Tollhead all the way to the back of the printer.
Cut the excess zip tie.
While moving the Printhead, ensure that the cable does not obstruct the movement of the XY axis.
If you are installing the GEN 2 upgrade along with the Prusa INDX conversion, return to the Prusa INDX GEN 2 article now.

Sheet metal back cover (1x)
xBuddy cover (1x)
Zip tie (2x)
M3x4rT screw (8x) you removed earlier
Be careful not to mix up the M3x4rT and M3x5rT screws, which you will need later for the door assembly.
Insert all loose ends of the PTFE tubes inside the printer.
Bundle the cables together and secure them with two zip ties. Do not overtighten the zip ties.
Before closing the electronics cover, check that everything is correctly connected.
Use the pictures as a reference to verify your electronics connections.
The electronics compartment is divided into two boards:
xBuddy board
xBuddy extension board
Carefully cover the xBuddy box by first sliding the bent part of the cover into the box.
Avoid pinching the cables and make sure to insert the cover parallel to the xBuddyboard.
Secure the xBuddy box cover using the six M3x4rT screws you removed earlier.
Align the rear sheet metal cover so that the cables can run through the "tray".
Place the rear sheet metal cover into the recess. Push it toward the printer, then move it upward to engage it.
There are four tabs that should engage into the printer’s chassis.
Insert the filament sensor cable to the cutout.
If you have a USB-C cable for the Buddy3D camera installed, route it through the lower cutout.
From the inside of the printer, secure the rear cover in place using two M3x4rT screws you removed earlier.

Thimble (8x) found in Tools bag
Spring 0.5 x 8.5 x 30 x 15 (8x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX bag
Spring 0.63 x 5 x 15 x 11 (16x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX bag
M3x12cT countersunk screw (16x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
INDX C1 Front profile (1x) found in the main box
Fully thread the M3x12cT screw into both holes of the Tool-holder, then remove the screw.
This creates a thread in the part, making the Tool-holder easier to install on the front profile later.
Position the Tool-holder with the countersunk holes facing up.
Insert each Thimble into the oval hole in part Tool-holder.
Insert a large spring (0.5 x 8.5 x 30 x 15) into each Thimble.
Insert two small springs (0.63 x 5 x 15 x 11) into the side holes of part Tool-holder.
Repeat the same procedure for all remaining Tool-holder parts.
In the correct orientation, place the Tool-holder against position 1 on the underside of the front profile.
Align the holes in both parts.
CAUTION: When placing the Tool-holder, make sure no spring is pinched against the front profile.
Secure the Tool-holder using two M3x12cT screws.
The screw forms its own thread in the plastic. Slight resistance is expected.
Grasp the Tool-holder and gently wiggle it. It must not be rigid - a slight, barely perceptible looseness is required.
Repeat the procedure for the remaining Tool-holder assemblies on the front profile, ideally in order 1–4, then 8–5 for easier handling.
Listed are the parts needed for the 8-tool version of the printer. For the 4-tool version, you will need half of the parts.
For the following steps, prepare:
Nozzle-seal-holder (4x) found in the Tools bag
Nozzle parking plate (8x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX
Nozzle seal (8x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX
M3x8rT screw (16x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
Slide a nozzle seal (silicone sleeve) onto each nozzle parking plate.
CAUTION: Handle with care! The edges of the nozzle parking plate are sharp and may cause injury.
Note the correct placement of the nozzle seal before attaching it to the Nozzle-seal-holder.
In the correct position, the holes align while the nozzle seal on the opposite side does not extend beyond the Nozzle-seal-holder.
Place the nozzle seal assembly onto the Nozzle-seal-holder so that the bent part of the Nozzle seal faces upward.
Attach the nozzle seal assembly to the Nozzle-seal-holder using an M3x8rT screw.
Turn all the Nozzle-seal-holders upside down; this is how we will install them in the next step. The bent part of the nozzle seal is now facing downward.
Install two nozzle seals on each Nozzle-seal-holder using the same method.
With the 4-toohlead version, start installing the nozzle holders from the same side as in the photo. Check the other side of the tooldock to ensure that you start from number 1.
Align the nozzle holder assembly with the holes at positions 1–2 on the front profile.
Ensure the nozzle seals are correctly oriented by matching the bent ends to the illustration.
From the other side, secure the nozzle seal holder assembly with two M3x8rT screws and tighten firmly.
The screw forms its own thread in the plastic. Slight resistance is expected.
Ensure that none of the nozzle parking plates are bent or damaged during the assembly.
Continue installing the remaining nozzle holder assemblies using the same method.
For the following steps, prepare:
INDX-C1-Vent-lever (1x) found in the Toolhead bag
INDX-C1-Vent-lever-holder (1x) found in the Toolhead bag
M3w washer (1x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
M3x8rT screw (3x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
Place the Vent-idler onto the Vent-lever-holder in the same orientation.
Secure it with an M3x8rT screw.
Place an M3 washer under the screw.
From the inner side of the front profile, align the part with the two holes.
Note the “TOP” marking on the Vent-lever-holder. It must face upward toward the bent section of the front profile.
From the opposite side (front) secure it with two M3x8rT screws.
For the following steps, prepare:
INDX-C1-grill-flexi (2x) found in the Top Cover Parts bag
INDX-C1-cover-latch (2x) found in the Top Cover Parts bag
INDX-C1-cover-knob (2x) found in the Top Cover Parts bag
Do not put the Top Cover Parts bag away; we will need more parts from it in the next step.
M3x12cT screw (4x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
M3x8rT screw (2x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
M3x10 screw (2x) removed earlier
Top cover (1x) found in the main box
Grille (1x) found in the main box
INDX-C1-hinge-cover-left (1x) found in the Top Cover Parts bag
INDX-C1-hinge-cover-right (1x) found in the Top Cover Parts bag
Turn the top cover upside down and attach the Hinge-cover from the bottom.
Secure each Hinge-top with two M3x12cT screws.
Make sure that you do not overtighten the screws.
Place the grill onto the top cover.
Note the correct position of the grill. The left side is prolonged! Ensure that it looks exactly as shown in the photo.
Before inserting the Grill-flexi parts, ensure that the grill is mounted correctly, with the prolonged side on the left.
Insert the Grill-flexi and hold them in position.
Secure the Grill-flexi in place with two M3x8rT screws.
Insert the INDX-C1-cover-latch into the top cover from the bottom. Note the orientation of the cover latch.
Attach the INDX-C1-cover-knob. Ensure that the knobs on the cover latch align with the holes in the cover knob. Press both parts together.
Secure the cover lock in place with the M3x10 screw.
Do not overtighten the screw. The lock must be able to turn.
Insert the INDX-C1-cover-latch into the top cover from the bottom. Note the orientation of the cover latch.
Insert the INDX-C1-cover-latch into the top cover from the bottom. Note the orientation of the cover latch.
Secure the cover lock in place with the M3x10 screw.
Do not overtighten the screw. The lock must be able to turn.
For the following steps, prepare:
Top cover back (1x) found in the main box
Hinge-base (2x) found in the Top Cover Parts bag
3x12sT screw (2x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
M3x25 screw (2x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
Nylon rivet (2x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
Spring 15x5 (2x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
Place the top cover back on the printer.
Secure the top cover back in place with two nylon rivets.
We recommend pre-cutting the Hinge-base with the screw before you install it. Insert the screw, tighten it, and then remove it from the printed part.
Place the Hinge-base near the front left hole in the top cover back.
Note that each Hinge-base part indicates which side it goes to. Ensure that the part is marked with an L (left).
Insert the 3x12sT screw from inside the printer and hold it in position.
Align the hole in the Hinge-base with the 3x12sT screw and connect the Hinge-base to the printer.
Tighten the 3x12sT screw while holding the Hinge-base in place.
Pictured is the 8-tool version. If you have the 4-tool version, the right PTFE-holder is not installed.
We recommend pre-cutting the Hinge-base with the screw before you install it. Insert the screw, tighten it, and then remove it from the printed part.
Place the Hinge-base near the front right hole in the top cover back.
Note that each Hinge-base part indicates which side it goes to. Ensure that the part is marked with an R (right).
Insert the 3x12sT screw from inside the printer and hold it in position.
Align the hole in the Hinge-base with the 3x12sT screw and connect the Hinge-base to the printer.
Tighten the 3x12sT screw while holding the Hinge-base in place.
Attach one Spring 15x5 on each of the M3x25 screws.
Place the top cover on the printer. Make sure that both hinges are positioned correctly.
Insert one M3x25 screw with the spring into each hinge from the inner side.
Use an Allen key to tighten the M3x25 screw on the left hinge. Do not tighten it completely.
Use an Allen key to tighten the M3x25 screw on the right hinge. Do not tighten it completely.
Slowly open the top cover all the way.
Make sure that the spring is able to retract and expand when opening the lid. This will hold the top cover open.
If the top cover does not stay open, check the tightness of the two M3x25 screws in the hinges and make sure the spring is in place.
For the following steps, prepare:
M3x4 screw (2x) that were removed earlier
The M3x4 screws were removed from the top front panel. Note that these two screws are black on some printer versions.
Nylon rivets (2x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
M3x4rT screw (2x) that were removed earlier
INDX Nozzle tool (8x) found in the INDX Nozzle tool box
Warning: Avoid touching or damaging the rectangular sensing area on the INDX Nozzle tool. Fingerprints, grease, or any damage can affect temperature readings and cause print issues.
Remove the two M3x4rT screws that hold the LED panel in place. Set the two screws aside; we will need them in the next step.
Support the LED panel with your hand when removing the screws, so it does not fall. Do not touch the LEDs and resistors on the LED strip!
Gently lean the LED panel on the left side of the printer.
Make sure that the LED cable is not damaged or pulled too hard during these steps.
Mount the assembled tooldock.
The left side of the tooldock has to be placed under the top profile.
The right side of the tooldock has to be placed above the top profile.
Secure the tooldock to the top profiles with one M3x4 screw on each side.
Secure the tooldock to the front of the printer with two M3x4rT screws (in the top holes).
Use the two M3x4rT screws you removed in the previous step to secure the lower part of the tooldock.
Mount the LED panel onto the inner side of the tooldock. Do not touch the LEDs and resistors on the LED strip!
The LED cable should reach the new position of the LED panel. If the cable is too short, gently and slowly pull on it to make it the correct length.
Use two nylon rivets to secure the LED panel in place.
Close the top cover.
This step is only required if you have a Buddy3D Camera.
Now is the right time to mount the camera in the front-left corner of the printer.
Use the dedicated installation guide:  Buddy3D Camera for CORE One Installation
The guide shows installation on the CORE One, but the procedure is the same. The camera attaches magnetically to the upper profiles of the printer.
Insert the PTFE tubes through the openings on the back of the lid, keeping the correct order.
Insert the PTFE tube from position 1 into the first opening from the right.
Repeat the same process for the remaining positions. Always make sure each PTFE tube is routed through the matching opening in the lid.
Open the top lid.
From the inside, fully insert the PTFE tube from the first opening into the INDX Nozzle Tool at position 1.
Try gently pulling the tube out of the collet to verify that it is locked in.
Repeat the same procedure for all tools in positions 1–4.
Place the INDX Nozzle tool on the first PTFE tube onto tool dock position 1 and align the magnetic pins on the tool with the openings in the tool dock.
Snap the INDX Nozzle tool into tool dock position 1.
Make sure both pins snap in fully and the tool sits perfectly flush.
Repeat the same procedure for the remaining tools up to position 4.
Double-check that the nozzle parking plates are in the correct position to seal the INDX Nozzle tool.
If you have the 4-tool version, skip to this step: Checking the tubes
Close the top lid. Insert the PTFE tubes through the openings on the back of the lid, keeping the correct order.
Insert the PTFE tube from position 8 into the first opening from the left.
Repeat the same process for the remaining positions. Always make sure each PTFE tube is routed through the matching opening in the lid.
Open the top lid.
Insert the PTFE tube from the rightmost opening into the INDX Nozzle Tool at position 8.
Try to gently pull the tube out to verify it is locked in the collet.
Repeat the same procedure for all tools in positions 8–5.
Place the INDX Nozzle tool on the last PTFE tube onto tool dock position 8 and align the magnetic pins on the tool with the openings in the tool dock.
Snap the INDX Nozzle tool into tool dock position 8.
Make sure both pins snap in fully and the tool sits perfectly flush.
Repeat the same procedure for the remaining tools up to position 5.
Double-check that the nozzle parking plates are in the correct position to seal the INDX Nozzle tool.
Pictured is the 8-toolhead version.
Check that the PTFE tubes are not swapped and that each tube is correctly routed to the corresponding tool position.
You can now close the lid and secure it by rotating the locks by 90°.
This is optional at this stage, as the lid will need to be opened again later during calibration.
Remove the empty cardboard box from the printer, as it will no longer be needed.
For the following steps, prepare:
Offset sensor sticker (1x) found in the Tool Dock Fan bag
The color of the offset sensor sticker might differ, but it does not affect the functionality.
Peel the protective layer off the offset sensor sticker and gently place the sticker onto the offset sensor.
Ensure that the sticker covers the whole sensor.
For the following steps, prepare:
Door panel assembly (1x) you removed earlier
M3x5rT screw (4x) you removed earlier
Top door seal (1x) found in the Top Door Seal bag
Peel away the bottom backing layer of the gasket to expose the adhesive surface.
Align the gasket on the front profile with the adhesive side facing the surface, then press it down to adhere.
If you had any issues with the shaft falling out of the hinge, assemble the hinge now, before mounting the door panel.
Insert the door panel fully into the hinges.
Ensure the door panel is oriented correctly, with the handle facing outward. Use the V-shaped cutouts on the inner side of the door handle as a guide.
Insert two M3x5rT screws into each Door-hinge to secure the door panel.
Secure the screws gently to avoid over-tightening or damaging the door panel.
For the following step, prepare:
CORE One+ sticker (1x) found in the INDX Update Stickers bag
INDX SN label (1x) found in the INDX Update Stickers bag
If you are installing the GEN 2 upgrade for the CORE One+ along with the INDX conversion, note that the "+" sticker is orange, not white.
Remove the sticker from the blue base.
On the door panel, align the sticker with the ONE and gently but firmly apply pressure to the sticker.
Carefully peel off the transparent layer and make sure that + is not peeling off.
Peel the Prusa INDX SN sticker off the base.
Place it on the back of the printer above the current CORE One/+ SN sticker.
You’re almost there. Take a break and get ready for the final chapter.
Eat eight gummy bears.
Now you have only one gummy bear left. Maybe more, depending on the factory filling. But we have one more reward coming, so keep the rest aside!
Congratulations! You have successfully upgraded your printer to the Prusa INDX edition!
Next, you only need to run the self-test and basic calibration.
Proceed to the next chapter.
